description:
A lane received unchanged at a self-tail-call back edge is not shared again.

Builds on fz-nml.29 version 3 (approved by the user 2026-11-18, relayed by JSON), which Optimize builds. Its ticket 2 gives binaries the shared mark at word 0. Its ticket 2b makes every share one inline load, test and store, and emits nothing for a value whose type holds no mark. Those two land first. They replace what this ticket used to propose (share only for list, tuple and struct, skipping binaries), which the mark on binaries would have made wrong.

What is left after 2b (compiler.md C6, machine.md M1):
- A tail loop re-shares its loop-invariant parameters at the back edge on every iteration. a == b makes 4 shares per call, 2 of them on parameters passed back unchanged. After 2b each is a load and a test of a mark that is already set.
- construct_call_ownership (src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs, at "fn construct_call_ownership") picks Share for an argument the continuation retains, even when the argument is the callee's own parameter at the same position in a self-tail call.

Fix:
- A self-tail-call argument that is the same parameter in the same position, with nothing in between that could unmark it, takes no Share. Nothing clears a mark once set, so a lane shared on entry stays shared.
- Interpreter and native agree: the rule lives in the ownership decision, not in either backend.

Asm first: the target listing for the a == b loop and a two-binary tail loop with no back-edge share.

Acceptance (bench, measured after 2b lands):
- the two-binary tail loop's slope falls by the back-edge shares' cost against the post-2b figure;
- a dump test shows no Share at the back edge for an unchanged parameter, and still one for a parameter that changed;
- every ownership fixture is unchanged on all three paths.

Blocked by fz-nml.29's ticket 2b once it is filed.

comments.text: Optimize (2026-11-18) agrees this ticket replaces their fz-nml.29 page ticket 2b, which they will not build. The seam, as the nml.29 page (v3) states it: there is one mark position (word 0). A share of a value known to be a binary is the same inline sequence in either layout. nml.29 adds binaries to the types that can carry a mark. The landing order is pending the user's ruling on nml.29's three questions; Optimize will tell Binary Handling when it changes.

Optimize's pinned-key probe: mark_published_ref_aliased + share cost 252 of 4,331 instructions per iteration. Trace: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/464fcf92-8f92-4767-a8fb-4e4eea4b6d45/scratchpad/pin12/iter.txt (scratch).

Trace location update: Optimize's pinned-key probe traces now live durably in /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-map-traces/ (iter.txt = a whole iteration of case_a_12; trace.txt = one lookup before the scan; the probe sources; and the lldb tracer script). The scratch path in the earlier comment is superseded.
